definitions.gloss: combined volume; omnibus edition; bound collection
definitions.explanation: A single volume that combines multiple separately published books, issues, or installments into one binding. Common in publishing for collecting magazine issues, manga volumes, or multi-part works.

examples.japanese: {雑誌|ざっし}の{合本|がっぽん}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought a bound collection of the magazine.

examples.japanese: {上|じょう}{下|げ}{巻|かん}の{合本|がっぽん}{版|ばん}が{発売|はつばい}された。
examples.english: A combined edition of the upper and lower volumes was released.

examples.japanese: {図書館|としょかん}では{古|ふる}い{学術誌|がくじゅつし}を{合本|がっぽん}にして{保管|ほかん}している。
examples.english: The library binds old academic journals into combined volumes for storage.

notes:
Compound of {合|がっ} ('combine; join') and {本|ぽん} ('book; volume'). The word describes the practice of binding multiple publications together. This can be done either by publishers (releasing an omnibus edition) or by libraries and collectors (binding loose issues together for preservation).

USAGE:
Can be used as a noun or with する as a verb ({合本|がっぽん}する, 'to bind together into one volume'). In the digital age, the concept extends to e-book omnibus editions that bundle multiple volumes into a single digital purchase, often at a discount.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {合本|がっぽん}{版|ばん}: combined edition
- {合本|がっぽん}する: to bind into a combined volume
- {合本|がっぽん}{製本|せいほん}: combined binding
- {電子|でんし}{合本|がっぽん}: digital omnibus edition

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {全集|ぜんしゅう}: complete works; collected works — a comprehensive compilation of an author's works, usually published as a set
- {選集|せんしゅう}: anthology; selected works — a collection of chosen pieces, not necessarily all from one source
- {単行本|たんこうぼん}: standalone book — a book published as a single volume, the opposite of a {合本|がっぽん}
- {文庫本|ぶんこぼん}: paperback; pocket edition — a small, affordable format; may or may not be a combined edition
